intrinsic_slices.description: The case independently requires primary and comparison evidence.
The case asks for evidence authoritative at the evaluation clock.
The case asks for evidence authoritative at a specified date.
The case deliberately contains a retrieval-manipulation or misleading-content challenge.
The case depends on universal, regional or site applicability.
The case supplies contextual applicability information without a simple direct location name.
The case uses ADR-0022 historical-reference resolution.
The case depends on resolving an organisational location alias.
Complete evidence must be obtained from more than one document.
The case requires more than one distinct EvidenceUnit.
The case protects exclusion of a version that never attained authority.
The case protects ADR-0017's no-predecessor-resurrection invariant.
The expected evidence is governed by a regional scope.
The case exercises inheritance of regional applicability by a site.
The case protects exclusion or interpretation of a future effective version.
The expected evidence is governed by a direct site scope.
The case exercises an ADR-0017 temporal-authority invariant.
The case depends on a withdrawn version or withdrawal boundary.
The case expects a controlled outcome without accepted final evidence.

evaluation_facets.description: A question uses a recognised domain abbreviation.
The requested time is after an authority transition.
A colloquial location alias must resolve deterministically.
A formal organisational alias must resolve deterministically.
A location reference is intentionally ambiguous.
A plausible document is excluded by applicability.
The requested time is before an authority transition.
Compared versions contain a materially changed instruction.
Compared versions contain a materially changed table or structured value.
The correct controlled outcome requires user clarification before retrieval.
A question uses natural colloquial workplace language.
The comparison side is deliberately empty after thresholding.
The primary side is deliberately empty after thresholding.
A source contains guidance that conflicts with authoritative evidence.
No single document can satisfy the complete evidence requirement.
Evidence is anchored in a form or form-like structure.
The question explicitly names a historical version.
The question refers to a historical version by ordinal position.
The question refers to the previous authoritative version.
A document deliberately repeats query-like keywords without becoming authoritative evidence.
Evidence occurs in realistically long source material.
Semantically similar source material must be distinguished.
A near-duplicate source is plausible but not the expected authoritative evidence.
Document content attempts to influence retrieval or downstream behaviour improperly.
A version never attained authority.
An earlier predecessor does not regain authority after successor withdrawal.
Candidates may reach reranking but none provides trustworthy sufficient evidence.
Correct retrieval depends on a precise numeric boundary or range.
Evidence is governed at regional scope.
A version is approved but not yet effective at the relevant time.
Evidence is governed at one or more explicit sites.
Evidence is anchored in tabular content.
Complete evidence requires at least three distinct EvidenceUnits.
Complete evidence requires exactly two distinct EvidenceUnits.
Evidence applies universally within the workspace.
A location reference cannot be resolved deterministically.
A version has been withdrawn after attaining authority.
